Ashish Khanna: 
Thank you, Sabri. Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining this call on our Q2 
FY '27 results. As we know, India's energy transition is gaining unprecedented 
momentum as the country rapidly scales renewable energy and electrification to 
strengthen energy security and advance its decarbonization and sustainability goals. 
With about 308 gigawatts of installed non-fossil fuel capacity, representing more than 
54% of total installed power capacity, the country is progressing rapidly towards the 500 
gigawatt target by 2030. 
 
India's peak electricity demand continues to reach new highs, reflecting rising 
consumption driven by industrial growth, electric mobility, data centers and the broader 
electrification of the economy. Against this backdrop, Adani Green Energy delivered 
another strong performance in H1 FY '27, crossing the significant milestone of 20 
gigawatts of operational capacity. Our 20.8 gigawatt portfolio supplied clean power 
equivalent to the needs of more than 4.4 million homes, while helping avoid 17.5 million 
tons of CO2 emissions during the period. 
 
Our operating and financial performance remained robust. Energy sales increased 32% 
year-on-year to 25.7 billion units in H1, supported by a 24% increase in greenfield 
capacity additions on Y-o-Y basis. Revenue from power supply in H1 FY '27 increased 
36% year-on-year to INR8,299 crores, while EBITDA grew 41% Y-o-Y to INR7,957 
crores, enabling us to deliver industry-leading EBITDA margin of 93%. The total 
EBITDA during H1 FY '27 was INR8,276 crores. If curtailment would not have been 
there, this EBITDA would have been close to INR9,000 crores.

The performance during quarter 2 was equally strong, with revenue from power supply 
increasing 45% year-on-year to INR4,019 crores, while EBITDA from power supply 
ending 51% higher Y-o-Y to INR3,835 crores, resulting in a strong EBITDA margin of 
92% during the quarter. 
 
Energy storage is becoming the next major pillar of our growth. During the quarter, we 
commissioned 3 gigawatt hour of battery energy storage at Khavda, taking our total 
installed storage capacity to 6.6 gigawatt hour. This capacity accounts for more than 
50% of India's operational BESS. We remain firmly on track to exceed 10 gigawatt hour 
during the year. While our maiden 500-megawatt pump storage project at Chitravathi is 
also progressing towards completion by year-end. At Khavda, the world's largest 
renewable energy plant, we have commissioned 10.8 gigawatt hour of solar, wind and 
hybrid capacity. 
 
Our focus on technology, digitization and advanced analytics continues to support high 
asset availability and strong operating performance across the portfolio. Looking ahead, 
we see significant opportunities emerging from growing needs for firm and dispatchable 
renewable energy, rising power demand from AI, data centers and hyperscalers 
alongside growing demand for integrated renewables plus storage solutions from 
commercial as well as industrial customers. 
 
Our investment in BESS is also helping mitigate curtailment challenges at Khavda by 
providing greater flexibility in managing renewable energy generation and enabling the 
utilization of power that would have been otherwise wasted. 
 
We will continue to closely monitor the developments on transmission infrastructure 
availability at Khavda. And at the same time, we have significantly accelerated the 
development of BESS to insulate ourselves from delays, if any, on transmission 
network. We remain focused on disciplined execution of our INR2.4 lakh crores capex 
program through FY '30, backed by securing new capacities under long-term contracts 
and prudent capital allocation. 
 
We remain committed to maintaining 13% to 14% ROE threshold by tying up capacities 
with AA+ counterparties. At AGEL, we remain neutral from a counterparty standpoint 
and will pursue opportunities that deliver high returns while offering long-term 
contractual visibility and desired credit quality. On sustainability, AGEL retained its 
number 1 global ranking in alternative electricity subsector by FTSE Russell for the 
second consecutive year. 
 
Our Khavda BESS project was also recognized as the largest project of the year at 
India Energy Storage Week 2026. Additionally, our Chitravathi, Gandikota and Tarali 
pump storage projects received the Best Construction Safety Excellence Award at the 
IBC Safe India Conclave and Awards.
